evidence.claim: Bloomberg’s analysis says Xi consolidated power by rewriting party rules, breaking succession norms, and relying on a decade-long corruption crackdown that remade the party leadership around his own allies.
evidence.title: How Xi Rewrote China’s Rulebook to Build the Party Around Himself
evidence.excerpt: Bloomberg’s analysis says Xi consolidated power by rewriting party rules, breaking succession norms, and relying on a decade-long corruption crackdown that remade the party leadership around his own allies.
evidence.source_locator: analysis text and section on purges and power plays
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Substantive contemporaneous analysis drawing on official sources and appointment data; strong for elite-control pattern, though still journalistic synthesis.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about the 2022 congress and the immediate run-up.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Xi because it concerns his rule, his rule changes, and his selected elite network.
contrary_evidence: The article is analytical rather than a single documentary finding.
It does not by itself prove personal enrichment or private self-dealing.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Xi secured a precedent-breaking third term and introduced a top governing body stacked with loyalists, with no clear successor and key figures tied closely to him.
evidence.title: China's Xi clinches third term, packs leadership with loyalists
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Xi secured a precedent-breaking third term and introduced a top governing body stacked with loyalists, with no clear successor and key figures tied closely to him.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs and description of the new Politburo Standing Committee
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting on the actual leadership line-up and its political implications.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Xi because it concerns the team he elevated and the succession rules he broke.
contrary_evidence: Some appointees were technocrats rather than pure ideologues.
Loyalist appointments alone do not prove personal corruption.

evidence.claim: Intelligence Online reported that all new Politburo and discipline-inspection appointees were subjected to unprecedented scrutiny by Xi's closest collaborators, and that some factions saw their influence wiped out.
evidence.title: Xi Jinping's new politburo emerges from lengthy and secret selection procedure
evidence.excerpt: Intelligence Online reported that all new Politburo and discipline-inspection appointees were subjected to unprecedented scrutiny by Xi's closest collaborators, and that some factions saw their influence wiped out.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specialist reporting on elite selection and secrecy; the summary snippet provides the key factual claim.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Xi's control over personnel selection and the narrow circle around him that performed the scrutiny.
contrary_evidence: The source shows scrutiny, but not independent scrutiny of Xi by outside institutions.
It is more about intra-elite vetting than public honesty.

evidence.claim: Intelligence Online reported that the Communist Youth League was being restructured because it had gotten in the way of Xi Jinping's political ambitions.
evidence.title: Xi Jinping brings Beijing's second-most influential body to heel before CCP Congress
evidence.excerpt: Intelligence Online reported that the Communist Youth League was being restructured because it had gotten in the way of Xi Jinping's political ambitions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specialist reporting with a direct claim on factional restructuring under Xi; the snippet is sufficient for the factual claim.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Xi because it describes a political reorganization driven by his ambitions and the neutralization of a rival base.
contrary_evidence: This is about factional power, not a direct financial conflict.
It still does not prove personal enrichment.

evidence.claim: The congress described Xi’s report as a political declaration and a program of action, and called on the party, military, and people to rally around Xi at the core of the Party Central Committee.
evidence.title: 20th CPC National Congress concludes in Beijing, Xi Jinping presides over closing session and delivers important speech
evidence.excerpt: The congress described Xi’s report as a political declaration and a program of action, and called on the party, military, and people to rally around Xi at the core of the Party Central Committee.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official congress record with explicit action-program language and formal adoption of the report and revised constitution.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong attribution because the resolution was adopted at the congress convened under Xi’s leadership and repeatedly centers Xi as the core.
contrary_evidence: This is institutional self-description, not an independent audit of delivery.

evidence.claim: China would speed up implementation of a package of policy measures to maintain stable economic performance, and the package was intended to improve the speed and effectiveness of policy implementation and ensure eligible firms and households benefited.
evidence.title: China to expedite delivery of policy package to keep economy stable
evidence.excerpt: China would speed up implementation of a package of policy measures to maintain stable economic performance, and the package was intended to improve the speed and effectiveness of policy implementation and ensure eligible firms and households benefited.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government implementation notice with concrete administrative instructions and timing.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate-to-strong attribution: the package was tied to the central policy orientation from the Central Economic Work Conference and Government Work Report, within Xi’s governing system.
contrary_evidence: The notice describes implementation intentions; it does not by itself verify local compliance or results.

evidence.claim: After special inspections in 12 provinces, the State Council said it would remove barriers, improve support measures, and better bring out policy effects for steady growth, market entities, employment, foreign trade, and investment.
evidence.title: China to remove bottlenecks in policy implementation to produce greater effects for keeping economic activity stable
evidence.excerpt: After special inspections in 12 provinces, the State Council said it would remove barriers, improve support measures, and better bring out policy effects for steady growth, market entities, employment, foreign trade, and investment.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official record of inspection and corrective follow-up, not just announcement.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate attribution through the State Council and central economic policy chain under Xi’s leadership.
contrary_evidence: The existence of inspections implies implementation problems remained significant.

evidence.claim: Chinese regulators outlined 16 steps to support the property sector, including financing for developers and special loans to ensure pre-sold home delivery, as part of a liquidity rescue.
evidence.title: Factbox-Key regulatory measures to stabilise China's embattled property sector
evidence.excerpt: Chinese regulators outlined 16 steps to support the property sector, including financing for developers and special loans to ensure pre-sold home delivery, as part of a liquidity rescue.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent factbox with specific policy mechanics and direct references to regulator notices, though still second-hand.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate attribution: the measures came from PBOC and CBIRC within Xi’s policy system; direct personal direction is not shown in the article.
contrary_evidence: The rescue package responds to a sector crisis that had been building since 2020, so it is partly corrective rather than wholly preventive.

evidence.claim: China was set to ease quarantine protocols and reduce mass testing after anger over the toughest COVID curbs fuelled widespread protests, marking a major shift in policy.
evidence.title: China set to loosen COVID curbs after week of historic protests
evidence.excerpt: China was set to ease quarantine protocols and reduce mass testing after anger over the toughest COVID curbs fuelled widespread protests, marking a major shift in policy.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent reporting on a major policy reversal with specific contemporaneous timing and direct causal context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate attribution: the shift occurred under Xi’s regime after public pressure; the source does not prove his personal authorship but does show state adaptation at the top level.
contrary_evidence: The shift appears reactive to public unrest, not a planned success from the outset.

evidence.claim: China’s 2022 R&D spending reached 30,782.9 billion yuan, up 10.1 percent year on year, with R&D intensity at 2.54 percent of GDP and basic research up 11.4 percent.
evidence.title: 2022年全国科技经费投入统计公报
evidence.publisher: 国家统计局 / 科学技术部 / 财政部
evidence.excerpt: China’s 2022 R&D spending reached 30,782.9 billion yuan, up 10.1 percent year on year, with R&D intensity at 2.54 percent of GDP and basic research up 11.4 percent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official statistical communiqué with exact numeric series and category breakdowns.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate attribution: strongly tied to Xi-era industrial and innovation priorities, though not uniquely attributable to one ruler decision.
contrary_evidence: Higher R&D input does not itself prove efficient conversion into output or broad productivity gains within 2022.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said China’s economy had uneven growth in 2022 and expected real GDP growth to slow to 2.7 percent before a 2023 reopening rebound.
evidence.title: China Economic Update - December 2022
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said China’s economy had uneven growth in 2022 and expected real GDP growth to slow to 2.7 percent before a 2023 reopening rebound.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Authoritative external macro assessment with clear date and quantitative forecast, though it is a projection rather than realized year-end data.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about the 2022 year and its end-state forecast.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate attribution: the Bank links the slowdown to pandemic cycles and policy support, but not to Xi personally alone.
contrary_evidence: This is a forecast and summary assessment, not a post-hoc audit of implementation.

evidence.claim: The IMF said China’s 2022 growth was expected to be below global growth for the first time in over 40 years, with pandemic restrictions, a deep real-estate contraction, and weak consumption as the main drags.
evidence.title: People’s Republic of China: 2022 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for the People’s Republic of China
evidence.excerpt: The IMF said China’s 2022 growth was expected to be below global growth for the first time in over 40 years, with pandemic restrictions, a deep real-estate contraction, and weak consumption as the main drags.
evidence.source_locator: abstract / context section in the Article IV page
evidence.source_confidence_reason: High-authority external assessment, but the accessible page is partly abstracted and the exact publication date is only available at issue level.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about the 2022 period and its macro conditions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate attribution: the IMF attributes the downturn to a mix of policy, pandemic, property, and external factors rather than to Xi alone.
contrary_evidence: The IMF statement is macro-level and does not isolate any single Xi decision as the sole cause.

Most of the anti-corruption and data-fraud material is system-level enforcement, not proof of Xi's own candor or self-dealing.
The strongest family-wealth context is pre-2022 and indirect, so its period fit for the target year is weak.
